blocks.md: This lesson covers the book's section on **The Operating Envelope**. Read the excerpt, then test yourself below.

blocks.source: Vol IV, Adversarial Verification, § The Operating Envelope
blocks.md: A mobile robot carrying a full payload down a warehouse aisle stops in a different distance when memory-bus contention delays its perception pipeline, when battery supply rails sag under acceleration, or when drive inverters heat up under sustained torque. Specifying the external operational design domain (ODD) alone therefore leaves the test conditions half-defined; an **operating envelope** couples those external conditions with the internal execution state of the computing, power, and actuation hardware.

questions.q: The section **The Operating Envelope** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Kish's effective sample size of the importance weights and a tail-coverage check reveal when a few heavy weights carry the estimate.
Failure probability cannot be read from falsification runs or naive Monte Carlo, so rates need importance sampling with a tuned proposal and tail magnitudes need weighted extreme value fits.
Timing the enforcer with on-target logging changes its timing, so verification uses non-intrusive hardware trace.

Each fault record binds a signed header (trial, claim, envelope point, injection, oracle digest, latencies, margins, verdict) to the independently retained trace, carrying evidence and its gaps to release.
